summary: Ran backend and frontend regression on preview URL. Most requested SHANE-AI branding, search, Atlas, Start Compass, Signal signup, metadata, streaming, Stripe, premium access, and overflow checks passed. One critical security/integration failure remains in runtime CORS behavior.

critical.issue: Runtime CORS responds with access-control-allow-origin: * for both allowed and disallowed origins, so strict-origin policy is not enforced.

integration_issues.issue: Browser console repeatedly shows 401 network errors from /api/auth/me for unauthenticated visitors (handled gracefully in UI but noisy).

action_items: Fix deployed CORS behavior to return only configured origins (no wildcard) and deny disallowed origins for preflight.
Optionally reduce noisy guest 401 logs from auth probe if desired for cleaner production console telemetry.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py appears configured for env-driven CORS origins, but deployed runtime behavior is still wildcard; verify active environment values and any ingress/proxy-level header overrides.
All newly tested subscriber, streaming, premium, and Stripe flows are functionally working on preview URL.
test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md seeded tokens: test_session_shane_free_2026 and test_session_shane_premium_2026.
seed_data_creation: Created test subscriber records (e.g., test_signal_idempotent@example.com and ui_signal_<timestamp>@example.com), plus additional mood/journal/message/booking records through regression tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite now has 26 tests; 24 pass and 2 fail, both CORS-only failures in test_subscribers_cors.py. UI automation validated logos in header/orbit/tarot/auth-callback, Atlas worlds/topics, global search flows, Start Compass all five intents, Signal duplicate idempotency, metadata/posthog config, and no horizontal overflow on 1920x800 and 390x800.
rca of the issue: Repro: OPTIONS /api/dashboard with Origin=https://neural-shane-1.preview.emergentagent.com returns 204 and access-control-allow-origin:*; same result for Origin=https://evil.example. Expected strict allowlist behavior. Likely causes: runtime env still providing wildcard CORS_ORIGINS, app not reloaded with latest env, or ingress/proxy injecting permissive CORS headers. Mitigation: inspect active runtime env + ingress CORS policy, remove wildcard override, ensure allowed-origin echo behavior with credentials, then rerun failing CORS tests.
